races.name: BOYLE Sports Money Back If 2nd To SP Fav Handicap

runners_data.name: Baggot Street
runners_data.note: Front-runner coming off a confidence-boosting 33-1 win but faces stronger pace pressure here with Plushy and Spiced Gold also wanting the lead
runners_data.comment: Ex Charlie Johnston; wears blinkers for the first time on yard debut
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well in defeat on multiple occasions for Charlie Johnston at 6f/7f; sported first-time blinkers when running out a surprise 33-1 winner on stable/seasonal debut at Navan (6f, yielding) 13 days ago; should go well again.

runners_data.name: This Guy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with solid recent form who should benefit from the expected strong early pace in this easier grade
runners_data.comment: Maiden looked on the verge of AW success during the winter, unplaced at Naas last Monday
runners_data.spotlight: Maiden was runner-up three times in a row at Dundalk during the winter; not as good in recent months; midfield in 6f Curragh handicap on latest but this is an ease in grade; Colin Keane takes over; high draw not ideal.

runners_data.name: Love Bomb
runners_data.note: Proven at this course and distance but has fading tendencies that could be exposed if the pace is too strong early
runners_data.comment: Won off 6lb lower last year, yet to fire this term, 3lb wrong, others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Won C&D handicap (yielding) last September off 3lb higher; yet to really fire this term but takes a big drop in class after a poor run at the Curragh 10 days ago; drawn widest of all.

runners_data.name: Plushy
runners_data.note: Natural leader with 0-10 record who may get outpaced for early position against Baggot Street
runners_data.comment: Some good runs in defeat on turf and AW, weighted to reverse Jan' form with Stone Bear
runners_data.spotlight: Record is 0-10 but has run well in defeat; placed on first two starts in 5f maidens last year at Bellewstown (good) and Cork (good to firm); excuses for Naas flop on latest as fly leapt the stalls; contender eased in grade.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: Prominent runner taking a significant drop in class after disappointing on soft ground in maidens
runners_data.comment: Well beaten both starts at Cork over 5f and 6f, qualifies for handicaps after this
runners_data.spotlight: Failed to fire in three maidens at 5f/6f on yielding/soft ground, the latest of those at Navan 13 days ago when beaten 11.5l into fifth; likely improver now handicapping; worth a market check.

runners_data.name: Spirit Above
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 58-day break making his turf handicap debut at shorter trip
runners_data.comment: No sign yet of winning potential, can only be watched in first turf handicap
runners_data.spotlight: Showed no signs of winning potential in maidens or on handicap debut at Dundalk (6f) on latest; can only be watched down in trip in first turf handicap.

runners_data.name: Spiced Gold
runners_data.note: Front-runner who faded badly behind Baggot Street last time and likely to repeat that pattern
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 3yo making handicap debut after 3 undistinguished runs as a 2yo; best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Three undistinguished runs as a 2yo; tailed off behind Baggot Street on handicap/seasonal debut at Navan 13 days ago; best watched.

runners_data.name: Hooves Your Daddy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with fading tendencies returning from Dundalk success but uncertain about turf form
runners_data.comment: Best effort came in Naas maiden but way out of form last twice in h'caps; off 206 days
runners_data.spotlight: Fair effort when fifth in Naas maiden in August (6f, good); struggled in following three runs but back from a break when runner-up at Dundalk last month (5f; had Love Bomb, Plushy and Lady Landhort behind); entitled to respect back on turf.

runners_data.name: Mini Cotai
runners_data.note: Closer who shapes well but tends to give way late, though the expected pace collapse could help
runners_data.comment: Not a bad run at Dundalk on penultimate, off since January, probably best watched
runners_data.spotlight: Modest form in good-ground turf maidens last year; shaped well over 6f at Dundalk in January when third; back from short break when giving way late on to finish fourth, beaten 1.5l in first turf handicap at Cork (5f, soft); 2lb wrong.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare with fading issues off a 36-day break facing stronger competition than her Dundalk win
runners_data.comment: AW win off 3lb lower in March, beaten off revised mark since, others appeal more
runners_data.spotlight: Sole success came in 6f Dundalk handicap in March off 49; came up short off revised mark twice since, one place behind Hooves Your Daddy over 5f at Dundalk on latest; 3lb lower on first turf handicap; in the mix.

races.paceDynamic: Baggot Street, Plushy, and Spiced Gold will all want the early lead in this 5f sprint, creating a fierce pace battle from the off. This aggressive early tempo will stretch the field and test stamina reserves over the final furlong. The strong gallop will set up perfect conditions for horses with prominent or hold-up styles who can finish strongly. This race shape clearly favours prominent runners and closers who can capitalize on the expected pace collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners engage in a speed duel through the early stages
scenarios.body: The pace will be unsustainable and create opportunities for horses tracking just behind or held up early to strike in the final furlong. This Guy and Mini Cotai are perfectly positioned to benefit from this likely scenario.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Baggot Street breaks cleanest and establishes an uncontested lead
scenarios.body: The recent winner can dictate terms without pressure and potentially kick clear, especially with his proven 5f form and confidence boost from his last victory. Plushy could also benefit if he secures the early position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Suits Prominents
scenarios.trigger: If the pace-setters are more restrained than expected in the opening two furlongs
scenarios.body: Prominent runners like Love Bomb and This Guy can track the leaders comfortably and have enough left for a sustained challenge. The race becomes more tactical, suiting horses with tactical speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Benefits Outsiders
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely with multiple horses stopping in the final furlong
scenarios.body: The race could open up for unfancied closers with fresh legs who avoided the early battle entirely. Cashel Blue drops significantly in grade and could surprise at big odds.

watchPoints.text: Spiced Gold could fold quickly if pressured early, potentially taking others down or creating interference
Watch the break closely as Baggot Street needs to secure an early position to avoid getting trapped behind the pace battle
Colin Keane on This Guy - his tactical riding could be crucial if the pace develops as expected
Love Bomb's tendency to fade in the finish could be amplified if she gets involved in the early pace battle
Monitor Mini Cotai for a sustained late run if the leaders tie up as expected in the final furlong

races.name: BOYLE Sports Money Back Meetings Every Day Fillies & Mares Maiden

runners_data.name: Youse Raven Mad
runners_data.note: Unknown style newcomer with decent breeding but no form guide to assess tactical suitability for this race shape.
runners_data.spotlight: Raven's Pass filly; 16,000euros yearling; half-sister to winners High Fibre and Granary Queen; dam 7.4f 2yo/1m winner (72), half-sister to Australian 1m4f Group 3 winner Caravan Rolls On; best watched.

runners_data.name: Courtlough Gula
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario but 253 days off and poor debut form are major concerns.
runners_data.spotlight: Sent off 200-1 for 7f Naas debut last September and failed to beat a single rival home.

runners_data.name: Dandymaria
runners_data.note: Unknown style but well-bred newcomer from good trainer whose siblings showed early speed ability.
runners_data.spotlight: Dandy Man filly; 23,000euros yearling; sister to Listed-placed 5f-6.5f winner Whistle And Flute (inc 2yo; RPR 106); dam unraced half-sister to 1m 2yo Group 2 winner Agnes Stewart and 1m5f Listed winner Sorrel; watch betting.

runners_data.name: Ruby Vega
runners_data.note: Unknown style with decent breeding but inexperienced 10lb claimer Ruby Kinkaid may struggle tactically.
runners_data.spotlight: Lucky Vega filly; 19,000euros foal; half-sister to 5f winner; dam unplaced, half-sister to 5f Group 3 winner Came From The Dark, out of Group-placed 7f winning half-sister to 6f Group 1 winner Pipalong; watch.

runners_data.name: Sioux The Boss
runners_data.note: Unknown style but expensive yearling with strong breeding suggests potential above maiden level.
runners_data.comment: Sioux Nation filly cost 70,000euros as a yearling; worth a market check on debut
runners_data.spotlight: Sioux Nation filly; 70,000euros yearling; half-sister to four winners inc Measure Of Time (French 1m1f-1m6f inc 2yo/Listed; RPR 102); dam unraced sister to 1m2f/1m4f Listed Flat winner and smart jumper Stage Affair.

runners_data.name: Rebel Wave
runners_data.note: Hold-up style benefits from expected steady pace but needs significant improvement on disappointing Naas fifth.
runners_data.comment: E280,000 New Bay filly, dam 7f US dirt winner, could go well, market best guide
runners_data.spotlight: New Bay filly's price rose from 110,000gns as a yearling to 280,000euros as a foal; looked in need of the run when fifth of eight on Naas debut (1m, good) 12 days ago; should strip fitter now.

runners_data.name: What About Us
runners_data.note: Prominent style perfectly suits this race shape and O'Brien's excellent strike rate adds confidence.
runners_data.comment: Second in a 7f maiden at Dundalk on debut, failed to show improvement on her second AW run
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for 160,000euros last May; two encouraging opening efforts when hitting the frame in 7f Dundalk maidens late last year; found only the Group 1-entered Glyfada too good at Killarney (1m, good) on return 17 days ago; the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Miss Moore Cen
runners_data.note: Unknown style but fading tendency and modest debut form suggest limited impact likely.
runners_data.spotlight: Very capable young trainer but will need to step up a lot on midfield finish at the Curragh (6f) on debut when behind Cactus.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits expected pace but showed little on Roscommon debut despite hooded application.
runners_data.comment: Half-sister to a winner at around 7f, stable's Flat wins typically with older horses
runners_data.spotlight: Made little impression in 7.5f maiden claimer at Roscommon on debut 11 days ago; hooded.

runners_data.name: Justiciar
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits race shape but disappointing recent form since promising Curragh debut undermines chances.
runners_data.spotlight: Top-rated in the field with a mark of 83; promise on Curragh debut (7f, good) last June when 1.5l third behind Composing (peak rating 110); disappointing since, including on handicap debut at the Curragh (7f) on latest; headgear needs to bring out improvement.

runners_data.name: Croi Gra
runners_data.note: Lead style with tactical advantage as only front runner but must settle better than previous keen racing.
runners_data.comment: Respectable debut at a big price in a Gowran race dominated by market leaders, can improve
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable debut when third at a big price in 1m Gowran maiden dominated by market leaders; raced far too keenly and built up big early advantage before weakening on next start at Navan (1m2f); drop in trip may help.

runners_data.name: Cactus
runners_data.note: Prominent style benefits from race shape but regressive form pattern and well-exposed nature are concerns.
runners_data.spotlight: Well exposed daughter of Wootton Bassett out of a mare by Galileo; regressive tail end of last year; fourth of 24 in 6f Curragh maiden (soft) on return; hard to be confident despite the pedigree, connections and being Aidan O'Brien's sole runner on the card.

runners_data.name: Hasita
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits tactical setup and eyecatching Cork third suggests return to form is possible.
runners_data.comment: Needs to step up on the form of two juvenile outings at the Curragh, yard's second string
runners_data.spotlight: Contested two very strong Curragh maidens last May/June as a juvenile; returned with eyecatching never-nearer third of 15 at Cork (6f, soft); wasn't given a hard time and every chance with Ben Coen back aboard if she handles quicker ground.

runners_data.name: Wearing Stars
runners_data.note: Prominent style fits race dynamics but mixed form across surfaces and distances creates uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed over 6f on AW; should come on from reappearance fourth at Cork (5f, soft)
runners_data.spotlight: Twice placed over 6f on AW late last year; fourth in 5f Cork maiden on reappearance; never in contention on 6f handicap debut at Naas last month; others are more likely for win purposes.

races.paceDynamic: Croi Gra is the only confirmed front runner in this field and will dictate terms from the start, likely getting an easy lead given her style and previous keen racing tendencies. With What About Us and Justiciar providing prominent support but no other genuine pace pressers, the tempo will be comfortable through the early stages. The lack of pace pressure means Croi Gra can control fractions, while prominent racers like What About Us, Hasita and Cactus can track into good positions. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and hold-up horses who can benefit from the expected steady gallop and finish strongly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running Success
scenarios.trigger: If Croi Gra settles better than her last keen performance and dictates comfortable fractions.
scenarios.body: The lack of pace pressure allows her to string the field out and kick clear in the straight, while her previous third at Gowran shows she has the ability when not over-racing. Her trainer Lupini is in good form and Leigh Roche can utilize the tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If What About Us and other prominent racers get the perfect trip tracking the lone leader.
scenarios.body: The steady gallop suits What About Us perfectly given her two encouraging frame finishes at Dundalk, and Joseph O'Brien's excellent strike rate gives confidence. The tactical setup allows prominent racers to conserve energy and outkick the leader late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too slow and hold-up horses get a strong finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Rebel Wave and Due In June benefit from a sprint finish scenario where their closing style can be maximized. The lack of early pace means hold-up horses aren't strung out and can deliver one sustained run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut Winner Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the newcomers has significant undisclosed ability and benefits from the tactical setup.
scenarios.body: The steady pace allows a well-bred newcomer like Dandymaria or Sioux The Boss to show their true colours without pace pressure. Their connections suggest potential above their maiden status.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Croi Gra over-races early again as her keen tendencies could compromise her tactical advantage despite having the lead to herself.
Monitor What About Us for market confidence as Joseph O'Brien's strong strike rate and her frame finishes suggest she could be well-handicapped.
Observe any significant market moves for the newcomers Dandymaria and Sioux The Boss as their breeding suggests potential above maiden level.
Check if Justiciar shows more enthusiasm early as his prominent style suits but recent disappointing efforts raise effort questions.
Watch for late money on Hasita as her never-nearer Cork third suggests she may have been given an easy time and could improve significantly.

races.name: BOYLE Sports Extra Places Every Day Handicap

runners_data.name: Imperial Dream
runners_data.note: Prominent runner suited by this trip and good ground, claiming jockey reduces weight significantly
runners_data.comment: C&D winner on quick ground in August 2024, only flashes of his best form last year
runners_data.spotlight: Close fourth over C&D at this meeting in 2024 off 74; last win at the Curragh (6f, good) in August of that year; has largely struggled for form since.

runners_data.name: Charming Whisper
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with strong good ground record but 62 days off and slow-starting tendencies concerning
runners_data.spotlight: Won five times when trained in Britain by Philip McBride; all those wins came on ground with good in the description; slowly away and always behind at the Curragh on latest; new headgear.

runners_data.name: Shoot To Kill
runners_data.note: Prominent style ideally suited to tracking Brains, talented claimer takes off valuable 5lbs
runners_data.comment: Won this last year, effectively 13lb lower here with rider's claim,  don't discount
runners_data.spotlight: Two wins last year on good ground for different trainers, including 7.5f Roscommon handicap off 80; now 10lb lower plus talented claimer takes off another 5lb; got his favoured ground when eyecatching third of 14 at Roscommon from tough draw 18 days ago; big chance.

runners_data.name: Amemri
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to form with winning experience at this distance
runners_data.comment: Recorded tenth win under rules' on AW last month; C&D winner last year off 5lb higher
runners_data.spotlight: Back to form when recording a tenth career win at Dundalk in March; has won three times on turf and finished runner-up of 15 at Limerick (1m, yielding) on latest when just in front of Minaun View; player.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but poor recent form makes him hard to fancy despite good ground preference
runners_data.spotlight: Three turf wins, the latest at the Curragh in 2024; added a 6f AW win last September; needs to step up considerably on the form of this season's four outings.

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Prominent runner in good form with 7lb claiming jockey, won at Leopardstown last year off similar mark
runners_data.comment: C&D winner last June off 2lb lower, has a bit to find with Monvoe on Limerick running
runners_data.spotlight: Enjoyed a good spell last summer, winning at Leopardstown (1m, good) off 1lb lower; fair efforts in defeat this year, including third at Leopardstown a fortnight ago; likely to be in the shake-up.

runners_data.name: Minaun View
runners_data.note: Prominent style but still a maiden after 15 starts despite some decent placed efforts
runners_data.comment: 0-14, decent run at Limerick latest, nicely drawn, place shout if gets in; reserve
runners_data.spotlight: Third runner for yard; maiden after 15 starts; one of her better runs when 3l third of 15 at Limerick (1m, yielding; one place behind Amemri) on penultimate; best work late on when fifth of 14 at Roscommon (7.5f, good) on latest; place shout.

runners_data.name: Dynamic Force
runners_data.note: Prominent early speed but veteran form has declined significantly this season
runners_data.comment: On a long losing sequence and lacks a recent run, very capable rider claims 7lb
runners_data.spotlight: Speedy in his early days, winning three times over 5f for Robert Cowell; runner-up when sent off favourite for this race (good) last year; 8lb lower now but on a long losing sequence and weakened at Leopardstown on return.

runners_data.name: Land Of The Giants
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent current form having won last start off lower mark
runners_data.comment: Stall advantaged over trip, expected to go really well
runners_data.spotlight: Second runner for yard; in good form on turf recently, with a breakthrough win at Ayr (1m1f, good to firm) off 63 at the start of the month; fairly treated back on home soil but below his best in two starts since, including Dundalk claimer on Tuesday.

runners_data.name: Una Matata
runners_data.note: Hold-up style returning to turf after excellent AW form, 7lb claimer valuable
runners_data.comment: Didn't land a blow a week ago from wide draw in handicap but respected back in a claimer
runners_data.spotlight: First turf run since September last year; excellent record on AW of late, winning four of her last 10 starts, three at this trip; one place behind Thaloria when third in 7f claimer there when last seen; tough mark back on grass.

runners_data.name: Eichan San
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with ability but winless in 8 starts, 7lb claimer helps his cause
runners_data.spotlight: Now 0-8 but has ability judged on his keeping-on fourth of 21 at the Curragh on penultimate (6f, soft); the drop to 5f was a bad move last time (outpaced) but can't rule out a big run over this trip.

runners_data.name: Goldsmith
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but 231 days off and poor form for current yard makes him hard to recommend
runners_data.spotlight: Third reserve; five AW wins when trained in Britain; mostly below form for this yard.

runners_data.name: Bay Of Dreams
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been tailed off in both starts for new trainer
runners_data.comment: Highly consistent in Britain last year, tailed off on stable debut when badly hampered
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice for James Ferguson last year, including on turf at Nottingham; tailed off in two starts for this yard, behind third-placed Faoladh at Leopardstown on latest.

runners_data.name: Thaloria
runners_data.note: Prominent runner effective on AW but poor turf record is concerning factor
runners_data.comment: Dundalk winner, needs to step up on the form of her Leopardstown run last month
runners_data.spotlight: Stepped up markedly on maiden runs when scoring on handicap debut at Dundalk in January over 7f; not as effective on turf and was completely tailed off in 1m Curragh handicap (good) on Sunday; eased in grade but others preferred.

runners_data.name: Lohengrin
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but dreadful recent form and brought down last time adds to concerns
runners_data.comment: Only win from 27 starts gained in a 7f maiden at Laytown, his trainer's local track
runners_data.spotlight: Won 7f Laytown maiden last September; poor winter form at Dundalk; brought down at Bellewstown on return; in rear at Navan and Roscommon; Colin Keane is 0-8 on him; looks vulnerable.

runners_data.name: Brains
runners_data.note: Only confirmed leader in field, gets ideal tactical setup despite being second reserve
runners_data.comment: Won over C&D at this meeting two years ago and ran well at Leopardstown on seasonal debut
runners_data.spotlight: Second reserve; seventh in this race last year; not beaten far on last two runs; in the mix.

runners_data.name: Burford Beauty
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but can get upset in stalls which is major concern in large field
runners_data.comment: Just fair form in h'caps but mark is dropping; fifth of 13 when last seen on turf
runners_data.spotlight: First reserve; just fair form in handicaps to date, including fifth over C&D; can get upset in the stalls.

races.paceDynamic: Brains is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 17-runner field and should get an uncontested lead through the early stages. With most runners holding prominent or hold-up styles, the pace will likely be moderate through the first half-mile before quickening significantly in the final two furlongs. The lack of early pace pressure means Brains can dictate terms and potentially steal a march, while the large field creates traffic concerns for hold-up horses. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can track Brains closely and hold-up horses with proven tactical speed to navigate the inevitable late congestion.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Brains gets soft fractions and kicks clear turning for home
scenarios.body: The veteran can control the tempo completely and use his experience to time his effort perfectly. Hold-up horses get caught in traffic as the field bunches behind the slow pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens from the 3f pole as prominent runners challenge Brains
scenarios.body: Horses positioned just behind the leader can respond immediately to any injection of pace and avoid the traffic problems further back. The moderate early gallop sets up perfectly for a sustained drive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Flies Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely in the middle stages creating a sprint finish
scenarios.body: Smart hold-up horses with tactical pace can weave through the field as it spreads out in the final furlong. The large field creates gaps for late closers with room to manoeuvre.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If significant interference occurs in the home straight with this large field
scenarios.body: Traffic problems and checking allow a horse with a clear run to emerge from an unlikely position. The race becomes a lottery favouring any runner who gets a clean passage.

watchPoints.text: Brains must be monitored closely for market support as the lone pace angle gives him a significant tactical advantage
Traffic problems are inevitable with 17 runners - watch for hold-up horses getting clear runs in the final two furlongs
Imperial Dream and Shoot To Kill both carry claiming jockeys taking off significant weight in a competitive handicap
Una Matata returns to turf after 63 days off following excellent AW form - her adaptation will be crucial
Land Of The Giants drops back in trip after winning over 9f last time but has winning form at this distance

races.name: BOYLE Sports Home Of The Early Payout Handicap

runners_data.name: Thistle Cross
runners_data.note: Front-runner who fades in the finish and showed poor turf form on seasonal debut
runners_data.comment: Couple of modest AW efforts late last year, easily overlooked now on turf debut
runners_data.spotlight: Couple of modest AW efforts late last year; completely tailed off on turf/seasonal debut; easily overlooked despite now handicapping.

runners_data.name: Andosky

runners_data.spotlight: Best effort when runner-up in Sligo nursery (6f, good to yielding) last year off 64; soundly beaten all three starts at trips ranging from 5f-7f this term; has to improve but handicapper's grip is loosening.

runners_data.name: Fontaine Khaled

runners_data.comment: Hint of promise under quiet handling last time and yard won this two years ago
runners_data.spotlight: Nice run in good-ground Curragh maiden last year; well held first two handicap starts but not beaten too far in much better race than this at Naas (6f) last month; wouldn't be too quick to dismiss her.

runners_data.name: Sand Art

runners_data.comment: Reserve; well beaten in three m'dens and no sign of improvement in h'cap last time
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in three maidens and no sign of improvement for switch to handicaps at Dundalk last time.

runners_data.name: Meriden

runners_data.spotlight: Never threatened in trio of maidens at 6f-1m on soft/AW; got going late when sixth of 13 on handicap debut at Ballinrobe (9.5f, good to yielding) three weeks ago; others preferred.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon

runners_data.name: Another Nice'day
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 191 days with previous cheekpiece form at this course
runners_data.spotlight: Respectable fifth at this course over 5f in her first handicap in September, staying on after taking a hold in first-time cheekpieces; failed to see out this trip at Dundalk next time; gelded ahead of return.

runners_data.name: Sweet Baby Zou
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse from strong O'Brien yard but yet to show winning potential
runners_data.spotlight: No sign of winning potential in three qualifying runs at 6f-1m2f on testing ground; looked in need of further when seventh of 14 at Roscommon (7.5f, good) on handicap debut but can't rule out for top yard.

runners_data.name: Dervo Annie
runners_data.note: Front-runner with Colin Keane booking who was well beaten on handicap debut
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten in trio of maidens at Navan/Dundalk over 5f-7f; market will provide clues
runners_data.spotlight: Long odds and soundly beaten in trio of maidens at Navan/Dundalk over 5f-7f late last year; never threatened when seventh of 13 on 1m Bellewstown handicap debut last month; booking of Colin Keane a plus.

runners_data.name: Queen Of Newark
runners_data.note: Prominent runner showing career-best form with recent third at Roscommon
runners_data.comment: Weak form last season and never involved over 5f at Dundalk last month, up against it
runners_data.spotlight: Weak form last season and never involved first two handicap starts over 5f; career-best when third in Roscommon maiden claimer (7.5f, good to yielding) 11 days ago but will need to pull out more back in a handicap.

runners_data.name: Stonyfalls
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse making handicap debut after 203 days off with 2yo rating
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten in four 7f maidens; has a more realistic opportunity now on handicap debut; market can reveal expectations after 203 days off.

runners_data.name: Imnotleavinyou
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with three consecutive runner-up finishes showing consistent late kick
runners_data.comment: Staying on second over longer trips of late; will want a strong pace at this shorter trip
runners_data.spotlight: Second runner for yard; placed in Naas nursery last term and finished runner-up all three outings this season at 6f-1m, each time staying on late on ground with an ease; quicker ground possibly not ideal but still shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Honey Dale
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who failed to stay 1m last time and carries claiming rider
runners_data.comment: Not a bad run at all when fifth over 7f here on soft, as  winner was thrown in
runners_data.spotlight: Not a bad run when fifth at Gowran last month (7f, soft); failed to see out 1m there last time on better ground; easy to look elsewhere.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with AW wins but poor turf record including recent Gowran flop
runners_data.spotlight: Has won over 6f/7f at Dundalk and runner-up over 1m there last month; yet to run a good race on turf, including when tailed off at Gowran (1m) last month.

races.paceDynamic: Thistle Cross and Dervo Annie will contest the early lead, with both confirmed front-runners likely to set an honest gallop over this 7f trip. Queen Of Newark and Fontaine Khaled should track the pace in prominent positions, while the large contingent of hold-up horses including Imnotleavinyou, Sweet Baby Zou, and Andosky will be anchored towards the rear. With two keen leaders and 14 runners on good going, the pace will be solid throughout, setting up the race perfectly for the hold-up horses who can finish strongly when the early leaders tire.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Thistle Cross and Dervo Annie duel early and maintain honest fractions
scenarios.body: The sustained gallop will stretch the field and exhaust the front-runners, allowing the patient hold-up horses to unleash their finishing kicks in the final two furlongs. Imnotleavinyou's recent consistency in staying-on efforts makes him perfectly suited to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Benefits Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders settles without serious pressure and dictates terms
scenarios.body: Queen Of Newark or Fontaine Khaled can track the tempo and strike when the pace quickens, avoiding both the early exertion and the traffic problems that may hinder the back markers. Queen Of Newark's recent career-best suggests improved form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Dervo Annie or Thistle Cross gets an uncontested lead and softer fractions
scenarios.body: The leader can conserve energy early and have enough left to resist late challengers, particularly if the hold-up horses are caught too far back in the large field. Dervo Annie's front-running style suits this tactical scenario better.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Favours Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If traffic problems and interference affect the fancied runners in the straight
scenarios.body: The large field creates opportunities for a well-positioned outsider to find clear running while others are shuffling for room. Stonyfalls returns from a long break with handicap debut conditions that could spring a surprise.

watchPoints.text: Thistle Cross and Dervo Annie could set unsustainably strong fractions if they engage in early speed duel
Imnotleavinyou may get caught wide or in traffic given his hold-up style in this large 14-runner field
Queen Of Newark's market movement after her career-best third will indicate stable confidence
Sweet Baby Zou represents Joseph O'Brien who has 10 winners from 60 runners in the last 14 days
Stonyfalls faces the market test after 203 days off to gauge yard expectations for handicap debut

races.name: His Majesty's Plate (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Tennessee Stud
runners_data.note: Quality prominent runner but 104 days off and Group 1 winner may need this return after long break
runners_data.spotlight: Group 1-winning 2yo made the frame last year in Epsom/Curragh Derbies and career-best when winning the Group 2 Prix Chaudenay (1m7f, very soft) at Longchamp in October; disappointing when last seen in Group 2 Riyadh contest in January, fading tamely on quick ground after forcing much of pace; demands plenty of respect on overall form.

runners_data.name: Carmers
runners_data.note: Reliable prominent style with good recent form, headgear suggests connections expect improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Won his first three races around this time last year, notably 1m6f Group 2 Queen's Vase; better again in defeat when second in 1m4f Great Voltigeur and fifth to Scandinavia in St Leger; not quite at same level on last month's seasonal return behind same rival in Navan Listed; visor now replaces blinkers.

runners_data.name: Dallas Star
runners_data.note: Natural front runner whose best form came leading, faces stiffer opposition than usual here
runners_data.spotlight: Won 1m2f Group 3 Ballysax Stakes in 2024 (1m2f, heavy); last win was at Dundalk early last year, having faced some stiff tasks since, career-best when front-running second to ready winner Scandinavia in Navan Listed last month; not as good behind same rival since under similar tactics in Group 3 Saval Beg; bit to find on ratings and step up to 2m looks a big ask.

runners_data.name: Layfayette
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up performer at 9 years old, won last start over 1m6f and distance increase suits
runners_data.spotlight: Winner of ten races, most recently last month's seasonal return in good-class Curragh conditions event, coming late in testing conditions (first attempt at 1m6f); never able to land a blow later same month on quicker ground in Saval Beg; first attempt at 2m.

runners_data.name: Alba Chiara
runners_data.note: Course specialist with all best form at Down Royal, significant weight advantage at bottom of handicap
runners_data.comment: Best form at Down Royal, a win and two seconds; will appreciate ground but lacks a run
runners_data.spotlight: All her best form has been here, notably winning 2m2f Ulster Cesarewitch last September off a lowly mark of 63; never sighted on last weekend's Curragh comeback run and tried blinkered here; proven stayer and likes the track but loads to find on ratings.

runners_data.name: Mont St Michel
runners_data.note: Front runner whose recent form is poor, last in both recent Flat attempts for new stable
runners_data.comment: Ex-Ballydoyle; 2m1f Killarney winner last August,
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Ballydoyle, for whom he won over 2m1f at Killarney last summer; brief spell hurdling for new connections before finishing last on both Flat outings, latest in Group 3 Saval Beg; out of depth again here.

races.paceDynamic: Dallas Star and Mont St Michel will ensure genuine early tempo over this 2m trip, with both horses needing to use their natural front-running tendencies. The presence of two confirmed leaders creates an honest gallop scenario where they'll either engage early or one will concede, but the pace will be fair throughout. Tennessee Stud and Carmers can track from prominent positions behind the leaders. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses like Layfayette and Alba Chiara who can exploit the pace and finish late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Dallas Star and Mont St Michel engage early and create strong tempo
scenarios.body: The dual pace angle sets up perfectly for closers to pick off tired leaders in the final furlong. Layfayette's proven late kick and Alba Chiara's course form become decisive advantages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one leader gets soft fractions while the other drops back early
scenarios.body: Tennessee Stud or Carmers can position perfectly behind moderate pace and kick clear before hold-up horses get organized. Their class edge over the leaders becomes telling.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Dallas Star gets uncontested lead with Mont St Michel settling
scenarios.body: Dallas Star can dictate comfortable fractions and prove hard to catch despite class concerns. His Group 3 winning form gives him enough quality to hold on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too hard early and prominent horses also tire
scenarios.body: Alba Chiara's course advantage and low weight become decisive when classier rivals hit the wall. Her Ulster Cesarewitch win here shows her effectiveness at the track.

watchPoints.text: Dallas Star getting uncontested lead could be dangerous given his front-running ability and Group 3 winning form
Tennessee Stud showing signs of needing the run after 104-day absence would compromise the market leaders
Mont St Michel breaking alertly alongside Dallas Star creates the strong pace scenario that suits closers
Layfayette's positioning in midfield early will indicate if connections plan typical hold-up tactics
Alba Chiara jumping from the gates sharply would suggest confidence in her Down Royal course form

races.name: BOYLE Sports Handicap

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist returning to form with Colin Keane booking, 49 days since last run could be sharp
runners_data.comment: Promising recent AW return; definite interest here off 8lb lower turf mark
runners_data.spotlight: Completed a hat-trick in handicap hurdles last summer before losing his way; decent run at Dundalk last month off 8lb higher AW mark so has to be of interest back on the turf (stamina proven).

runners_data.name: Pons Aelius
runners_data.note: Prominent runner trying tongue-tie on career-low mark, unexposed apprentice takes valuable weight off
runners_data.comment: Six-time winner at up to 2m in Britain but hasn't shown much for Donegal yard
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time winner at up to 2m in Britain but yet to hit any sort of form for current yard; career-low mark and tongue-tie tried so don't rule out.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with course form here, unlucky last time and remains open to improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Sole win came here last September (1m5f, good) but numerous placings include this term at Sligo; not much luck in running at Leopardstown on latest so remains of interest, especially given his record here.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner wearing tongue-tie, holds key to race but stamina unproven over this 2m trip
runners_data.comment: Another good effort when fifth of 19 at Leopardstown on Friday; first reserve
runners_data.spotlight: Three wins last year, two over hurdles and 1m4f Killarney Flat handicap off 59; recent Flat return was encouraging at Leopardstown although remains unproven over this extended trip.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden in good form, staying-on third last start suggests 2m will suit perfectly
runners_data.spotlight: Remains a maiden under both codes but running well of late, most recently staying-on third over 1m5f at Leopardstown (good); shortlisted.

runners_data.name: Among The Pines
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 233-day break with trainer change, warning flag for fading in finishes
runners_data.comment: Little of note last year; bought for small money and remains badly handicapped
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly raced maiden wasn't sighted in three maidens last year and last of 17 on handicap debut at Navan in October (upset in stalls), trained then by Michael Grassick; big step up in trip for seasonal/yard debut and best watched.

runners_data.name: Our Lucky Lady
runners_data.note: Hold-up hurdler dropping to lowest-ever mark, 269 days off Flat but won over trip before
runners_data.comment: Hurdles winner but little of late on Flat so hard to fancy; hood tried
runners_data.spotlight: Better hurdler, winning Sligo maiden (2m2f, good to yielding) in October, just okay run in handicap at Punchestown festival on latest; precious little of note on the Flat last year, tried hooded now on return and may improve.

runners_data.name: Synchronize
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden with poor handicap record, limited appeal returning to Flat after hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Dual-purpose maiden showed some ability in maiden hurdles but has been poor in handicaps; of limited appeal back on the Flat.

runners_data.name: Velvet And Vine
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 500-day absence, stamina major question mark at 2m
runners_data.comment: Maiden absent since early last year; career-low mark but hard to be confident in
runners_data.spotlight: 16-race maiden had been running okay in 1m4f AW handicaps last winter; back from a break with stamina to prove.

runners_data.name: Lisnadill
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was placed for previous yard, well held twice since trainer change
runners_data.comment: Narrow defeat when favourite at Naas (10.5f) for previous yard; markedly up in trip
runners_data.spotlight: Placed twice for Andy Oliver last summer, including a narrow defeat at Naas (10.5f, good); after a long layoff, well held on both starts for current yard this term on much softer ground (headgear combination tried on latest now ditched); return to better ground could see an improvement.

runners_data.name: Edge Of Darkness
runners_data.note: First reserve hold-up type whose form is declining rapidly, fading tendency worrying sign
runners_data.comment: Irish form is moderate in both codes, a tad better when beaten 6l (led) at Navan latest
runners_data.spotlight: First reserve; four-time winner over 1m4f back in the day in Britain; nothing like that sort of form for current yard, mark rapidly descending of late.

runners_data.name: Al What
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden coming off Tuesday's fall, previous third under today's claimer was solid effort
runners_data.comment: Down the field on hurdles debut at Killarney, fair Flat run at a modest level last week
runners_data.spotlight: Dual-purpose maiden didn't get beyond the first (swerved and unseated) at Ballinrobe on Tuesday; previous Roscommon Flat third under today's rider was a solid run so don't rule out.

runners_data.name: Miners Cabin
runners_data.note: Hold-up 4-year-old never sighted on handicap debut, big step up required here
runners_data.comment: Very modest form in maidens, transformation needed to feature on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Quite lightly raced 4yo never sighted on recent handicap debut at Leopardstown; good bit to find with a couple of today's rivals on that run.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer fresh from AW success, tongue-tie applied and apprentice claim helps
runners_data.comment: Recent AW second; unexposed hurdling, clearly in good heart and could go well
runners_data.spotlight: AW winner went close at Wolverhampton (1m6f) 18 days ago; due to run over hurdles at Wexford on Wednesday.

runners_data.name: Timandi
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden returning from 75-day break, better ground conditions should help significantly
runners_data.comment: Yet to trouble the judge in 12 attempts over various trips; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: 12-race maiden returned from AW campaign when never counting over inadequate 1m at the Curragh in March (heavy); given a break since and ground more in her favour here; stamina unproven.

runners_data.name: Sioux Grit
runners_data.note: Second reserve absent two years with blinkered headgear change, 8lb wrong at weights
runners_data.comment: Rated a meagre 32 so 8lb wrong here and hasn't run in two years; reserve
runners_data.spotlight: Second reserve; 0-18 and absent two years; 8lb wrong here.

runners_data.name: Bang Po
runners_data.note: Third reserve whose form has collapsed since 2023 win, 9lb out of handicap here
runners_data.spotlight: Third reserve; nothing of any substance since 2023 Killarney win; 9lb wrong.

races.paceDynamic: Tassarolo is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate a sustainable gallop without early pressure in this large handicap field. The prominent group of Pons Aelius and Velvet And Vine may track closely, but the majority are hold-up horses who will need the pace to develop. With 13 of 17 runners employing hold-up tactics, the race will develop into a cavalry charge from the back, creating a premium on horses with tactical speed and those who can position well mid-race. This shape strongly favours prominent racers and those hold-up horses with proven finishing kicks, while penalising one-paced plodders who rely on a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Setup
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo leads uncontested and maintains an even gallop throughout
scenarios.body: The large field will bunch up turning for home, creating a messy sprint finish that favours horses with tactical pace who can avoid trouble. Hold-up horses with finishing speed like Jurality and Mephisto can weave through to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Group Pressure
scenarios.trigger: If Pons Aelius or other prominent runners challenge Tassarolo mid-race
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field and creates a more genuine test of stamina over the 2m trip. This setup benefits proven stayers who can sustain their effort like Tassarolo himself and any hold-up horse with stamina reserves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Crawling Early Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Tassarolo goes too slowly early with no pressure applied
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the 3f pole with minimal stamina test, favouring horses with the best turn of foot regardless of trip preferences. Short-priced favourites with class like Mephisto and those who've shown speed recently get first run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates significant interference in the straight
scenarios.body: Early positioned horses avoid the worst of the trouble while many fancied runners get hampered or checked. Those prominent early like Pons Aelius and any hold-up horse drawn wide with room to manoeuvre benefit from cleaner passages.

watchPoints.text: Tassarolo must handle the 2m trip as his stamina is unproven beyond 1m4f despite controlling the early pace
Among The Pines returning from 233 days off with new trainer after being last of 17 on handicap debut
Multiple hold-up horses including Miners Cabin, Al What and Edge Of Darkness show concerning fading tendencies in recent runs
Pons Aelius trying tongue-tie for first time on career-low mark with inexperienced apprentice jockey
Fine Print due to run over hurdles Wednesday at Wexford which could impact participation here

races.name: BOYLE Sports Daily Racing Rewards Handicap

runners_data.name: Misty Cove
runners_data.note: Front runner likely to get easy lead but needs to prove he can sustain effort when challenged
runners_data.comment: Two fair AW runs, although form of Kempton third over 1m3f in January hasn't worked out
runners_data.spotlight: Couple of okay AW runs over the winter and reappeared for winning turf/handicap debut early this month, making most over this trip at Sligo (yielding-to-soft); 3lb rise okay, should go well again.

runners_data.name: Chapel Lane
runners_data.note: Hold-up type returning from 232-day break, needs everything to fall right from back of field
runners_data.spotlight: Improved on latter of three maiden runs in second half of last season, rallying third in first-time visor (left off here) over a mile at Thurles; good chance he'll improve further at this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Eniac
runners_data.note: Strong closer who showed promise on handicap debut, 5lb claimer takes off useful weight
runners_data.comment: Best maiden run came here (1m), should stay this far, bred to be better than opening mark
runners_data.spotlight: Opening handicap effort earlier this month offered plenty of encouragement, coming home strongly after not clear run to finish fourth behind a progressive type over 1m4f; drop in trip may not be ideal but major player nonetheless with likely more to offer and rider claims a valuable 5lb off top weight.

runners_data.name: Harmani
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with Colin Keane up, ideally positioned to track the leader and strike late
runners_data.comment: Handicap debutant, promise in maidens, sharper for latest, should stay 1m
runners_data.spotlight: Twice beaten favourite in maidens following promising 2yo debut; more like it on handicap debut early this month when good second in Cork apprentice event over a mile; shapes as though this longer trip will suit.

runners_data.name: Pierre Grosse
runners_data.note: Proven over this trip with solid form, 5lb apprentice claim makes him competitive off 80 rating
runners_data.spotlight: Improved for step up in trip when placed in 1m2f Leopardstown handicap on last month's return; similar RPR when clear second to a ready winner in Naas rated contest early this month; place claims again.

runners_data.name: Another Day Done
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in first-time visor, 47 days off may need this run despite Dundalk win
runners_data.spotlight: Nicely improved in first-time visor to handsomely win 1m Dundalk handicap in January (beating a subsequent winner); not clear run and hung right over same C&D 10 days later; not certain he stayed today's trip at Leopardstown last time (over 2l off Pierre Grosse at level); gelded since and visor back on (replacing cheekpieces worn latest).

runners_data.name: Oust
runners_data.note: Prominent type who showed improved form when dropped back to this trip last time
runners_data.comment: Appeared not to stay 1m5f at Ballinrobe last time, this may be closer to his best trip
runners_data.spotlight: Drop back to this trip at Roscommon recently seemed to suit when third under a positive ride; more likely needed.

runners_data.name: Sutton Hoo
runners_data.note: Likes this distance and sound ground, 91 days since last run is a concern for sharpness
runners_data.comment: Returns with yard in red-hot form and is half-brother to two AW winners; check betting
runners_data.spotlight: Nicely improved for step up to today's trip at Dundalk in February, clear with second in winning maiden; seemingly likes a sound surface so could have more to offer here back on turf for handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Rapide Vega
runners_data.note: Improving type making handicap debut off high mark, step up in trip is unknown quantity
runners_data.spotlight: Has improved in each of three runs, notably last month's Gowran return when fifth of 15 (1m, soft); upped in trip now for handicap debut off a high enough mark.

runners_data.name: Chestnut Palace
runners_data.note: Struggled over 1m4f last time, drop back to 1m2½f should suit better
runners_data.comment: Handicap debutante, just mild promise in maidens, this trip a query on breeding, watch
runners_data.spotlight: Just mild promise in three maiden runs before Leopardstown handicap debut earlier this month, seemingly not getting home over 1m4f; drop back in trip to suit but may not reverse form with Eniac.

runners_data.name: Vantage Code
runners_data.note: Well-beaten on seasonal return, big price reflects poor recent form
runners_data.comment: Big price for all three maiden starts at two, has been gelded, market may  provide a clue
runners_data.spotlight: Big price for all three maiden starts at two (some promise second occasion at Thurles), and again when never sighted on seasonal return in Curragh handicap last month; return to better ground may suit, any market support worth heeding.

runners_data.name: Lord Aus
runners_data.note: Slow starter with finishing concerns, needs to overcome stalls issues
runners_data.comment: Slowly away both starts at Navan and Gowran, may need more time and experience
runners_data.spotlight: Slowly away from the gates in all three maidens this spring when never featuring, upset in stalls latest; potential improver upped in trip for handicap debut but may need more time.

runners_data.name: Grey Intentions
runners_data.note: Cheekpieces first time, has shown little in four starts to date
runners_data.comment: Handicap debutante, best maiden run on latest, watch unless the market speaks
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't really count on recent handicap debut over a mile at Cork; longer trip may suit but lots to find with Harmani on that run; cheekpieces tried.

races.paceDynamic: Misty Cove is the only confirmed front runner and will dictate a sustainable pace without pressure through the early stages. The prominent runners Harmani, Oust and Sutton Hoo will track the leader while the majority of the field consists of hold-up horses who need to be produced late. With limited early pace and a large contingent of closers, this sets up as a tactical affair that will become a sprint from the 3-furlong pole. This race shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position close to the pace and have something left to kick, as the hold-up horses will struggle for room and clear runs in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Misty Cove maintains a steady tempo and the prominent horses get first run
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows Harmani, Oust and Sutton Hoo to travel comfortably in behind before striking decisively in the straight. The hold-up majority gets caught in traffic as these handily-placed runners skip clear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and the closers get lucky with gaps
scenarios.body: The tactical nature allows the better hold-up horses like Pierre Grosse and Eniac to weave through and deliver their finishing kicks. Their class and late turn of foot proves decisive when the race becomes a pure sprint home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Misty Cove gets soft fractions and kicks again turning for home
scenarios.body: The lack of early pressure allows the leader to conserve energy before quickening decisively in the straight. The closers are caught flat-footed by the change of pace while the prominent horses can't match the leader's renewed effort.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is funeral-slow and causes a bunched finish
scenarios.body: The crawling tempo creates a cavalry charge finish where any horse can win depending on luck in running. The race becomes a lottery with positioning and gaps more important than ability or running style.

watchPoints.text: Lord Aus has been slowly away in all three runs this year and could be left with too much to do again
Another Day Done hasn't run for 47 days and may need this outing despite wearing the first-time visor
Sutton Hoo returns after 91 days off and needs to prove his Dundalk maiden form translates to turf
The pace could collapse completely with only Misty Cove showing early speed, creating a messy finish
Several horses making handicap debuts including Rapide Vega and Lord Aus add unpredictability to the outcome

races.name: BOYLE Sports Best Odds Guaranteed Maiden

runners_data.name: Nermal
runners_data.note: Made good use of wide draw at Dundalk second start, prominent racer suited by likely uncontested early pace
runners_data.comment: Cheap purchase ran a solid fifth of 14 on C&D debut; more needed from very wide draw
runners_data.spotlight: Both runs came over 1m at Dundalk in January, improvement second occasion when made plenty of use of from a wide draw in chasing home a strong favourite; not sure this longer trip will suit but open to more improvement than most and a contender if staying.

runners_data.name: Maxminelli
runners_data.note: Definite step forward in first-time tongue-tie at Ballinrobe, prominent style perfect for tracking Divelment
runners_data.comment: Promise at Dundalk last year, heavy may not have suited latest, tongue tie on, chance
runners_data.spotlight: Definite step forward in first-time tongue-tie in similarly-rated Ballinrobe maiden early this month, putting it up to all-the-way winner final furlong when beaten a neck over just short of this trip (good-to-yielding); major player.

runners_data.name: Moon Vega
runners_data.note: Long absence since winter juvenile form, bred to improve but 170 days off track is concerning
runners_data.spotlight: Mild promise on first of two juvenile AW runs last winter; bred to improve with time.

runners_data.name: Teologia
runners_data.note: Improved latest when coming from back to chase home stablemate, hold-up style needs strong pace to aim at
runners_data.spotlight: Definite step forward on latest when coming from good bit back to chase home a stablemate in Ballinrobe claimer over just shy of this trip, despite running green; cheekpieces now added and major player.

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Shaped well over this trip behind Divelment on AW, hold-up tactics require late room in big field
runners_data.spotlight: Shaped encouragingly on second AW outing for Alan McIntyre over the winter, still looking green when fourth over today's trip (Divelment 0.75l ahead in third) in first-time cheekpieces; since joined Gordon Elliott and could go well (cheekpieces left off).

runners_data.name: Gatlinburg
runners_data.note: Recent Killarney fourth showed improvement, but warning sign of fading in finish could repeat
runners_data.comment: Has shown only modest ability in maidens, this longer trip may help to produce improvement
runners_data.spotlight: Recent Killarney handicap fourth (1m3f, good) a definite step in the right direction and won't have to improve too much more to play a role here back in ordinary maiden; headgear combination tried.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Funk
runners_data.note: Marked step up to 1m2½f from 7f-1m career, hold-up style unproven at extended trip
runners_data.comment: Leopardstown fifth was a small step in the right direction, can feature in a weak race
runners_data.spotlight: All four runs have been over 7f/1m, showing mild promise in Leopardstown maiden but no improvement dropped to claiming company latest; marked step up in trip here.

runners_data.name: Divelment
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with proven stamina over trip, uncontested lead could prove decisive
runners_data.comment: Rated 69, best treated by race conditions, new headgear combo, the one to beat if fit
runners_data.spotlight: Placed twice in maidens at Roscommon last year and again twice over this trip on the AW early this year; overdid the forcing tactics when disappointing in Ballinrobe claimer on latest, claimed afterwards for 5,000euros; definite chance on his best form.

runners_data.name: Kingcharles
runners_data.note: Modest recent form and fading tendency makes him vulnerable in competitive maiden
runners_data.comment: Always behind on Navan debut last month, easily passed over
runners_data.spotlight: Couple of modest runs of late, likely to need more time and handicaps.

runners_data.name: Tavarua
runners_data.note: Both runs came on soft ground over shorter, needs significant improvement on good going
runners_data.spotlight: Both runs last month came in soft-ground Gowran maidens over a mile; this longer trip should suit but good bit of improvement required.

runners_data.name: Amrum
runners_data.note: Half-brother to Siskin but looked limited in three maidens, better suited to handicaps
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to Irish 2,000 Guineas winner Siskin, no sign of winning potential so far
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to Irish 2,000 Guineas winner Siskin; has looked limited in three maiden runs this spring and looks a more likely one for handicaps although this grade of maiden offers possibilities.

runners_data.name: Avec Grand Plaisir
runners_data.note: Okay maiden form suggests handicap horse rather than maiden winner
runners_data.comment: Soundly beaten in maidens at the Curragh and Leopardstown five months apart
runners_data.spotlight: Just okay runs this term in maidens at Leopardstown and Roscommon; another for whom handicaps beckon.

runners_data.name: Second Line
runners_data.note: Failed to stay 1m2f second start, distance concern over today's longer trip
runners_data.comment: Excuse for a poor run at two, hard to make a case for him based on a Dundalk outing
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't troubled the judge in three runs, second occasion not looking to stay 1m2f; needs to improve plenty.

runners_data.name: Espritroyale
runners_data.note: Improved for yard change but took backward step latest, inconsistent profile
runners_data.comment: Better effort on stable debut latest, worth a market check in first handicap
runners_data.spotlight: No show in two maidens for Sheila Lavery last year; improved effort in 6f Curragh maiden on debut for this yard in March but took a backward step in Roscommon handicap since; big step up in trip here (half-sister to 1m4f winner).

races.paceDynamic: Divelment is the sole confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms from the outset, likely establishing a steady but uncontested lead through the early phases. With most of the field preferring hold-up tactics (Teologia, Gatlinburg, Cosmic Funk, Sonny Corleone), the early pace will be comfortable rather than fierce. The real race will develop from the home turn as the hold-up brigade look to close the gap, but Divelment's uncontested early advantage could prove decisive. This tactical setup clearly favours front-running and prominent racers who can track the leader without pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Divelment Controls Tempo
scenarios.trigger: If Divelment establishes an uncontested lead and maintains a sustainable pace throughout
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace pressure allows him to dictate ideal fractions and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still organising their challenges. His prior AW placings over this trip demonstrate stamina for a strong finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Swarm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent racers fail to track Divelment closely enough early on
scenarios.body: The conservative early pace sets up a cavalry charge finish where the strongest stayers prevail over the final two furlongs. Teologia's recent improved form and Gatlinburg's step forward at Killarney position them perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Maxminelli or Nermal can sit perfect stalking positions behind Divelment
scenarios.body: The tongue-tie improvement for Maxminelli or Nermal's wide-draw experience from Dundalk allows them to time their challenge perfectly in the straight. They get first run on the hold-up horses while having Divelment's measure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Divelment goes too fast early or the prominent horses fail to make their presence felt
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure stamina test where the longest-priced hold-up horses with questionable form suddenly become competitive. Fresh legs and natural improvement carry the day over tactical positioning.

watchPoints.text: Divelment could steal this if allowed uncontested lead by prominent racers failing to track him closely
Maxminelli's tongue-tie improvement may not translate from Ballinrobe claimer to stronger maiden company
Moon Vega returning from 170-day break could either show natural improvement or need the run
Several hold-up horses with fading tendencies (Gatlinburg, Second Line, Kingcharles) may disappoint again
Large field of 14 runners creates potential traffic problems for hold-up horses requiring late room
